clauses.reason: Terminated on 1933-10-20, the date the order issued: the order only denies an application ('do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be, and it is hereby, denied'), a one-time determination that commands nothing afterwards and is exhausted by performance on its own date. Actor: EO 6346 itself; the cited text is the order's own operative sentence. The applicants' continuing obligation under the minimum-wage provision is the code's own operation, which ended with the repeal on 1935-06-14 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113, recorded as a later event); it is not a surviving command of this denial. Schechter (1935-05-27) is a validity characterization and not an end date.

research_rationale:
EO 6346 (October 20, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) is read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6346-the-matter-the-application-the-greensboro-lumber-company-and-h-taylor.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; APP node 362174). APP page check under AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with the same sha256 (9edd3279...) has the heading 'Executive Order 6346—In the Matter of the Application of the Greensboro Lumber Company and H. A. Taylor, for Certain Exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries' and date 1933-10-20; number, subject and date agree with the text ('The White House, October 20, 1933'); and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The text is complete. Identity: the census register and the WPA 1944 list ('Application of Greensboro Lumber Co. and H. A. Taylor for certain exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries denied. II NRA Codes 696.') agree. original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. Operative command: the order denies one application for an exemption from the minimum-wage provision of the Lumber and Timber Products Industries code: 'do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be, and it is hereby, denied.' It approves nothing, amends nothing and grants nothing. Clause inventory: the machine inventory (one clause, the operative paragraph) is accepted. First end: the clause is a one-time determination exhausted by performance on its own date, 1933-10-20, when the denial issued; the order commands no person to do anything afterwards. The applicants' continuing obligation to obey the minimum-wage provision was the code's own operation, governed by the order approving the Lumber code (EO 6255, August 19, 1933), not a surviving command of this denial. Later event: S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved 1935-06-14, repealed in section 2 'all the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113); after that date the code the applicants had been refused relief from no longer had section 3 enforcement effect. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERSYL, SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERDEL, SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG). June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936 (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA2C, SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113).

savings.reason: The denial's own effect, the refusal of the exemption, was completed on 1933-10-20. The applicants' obligations under the minimum-wage provision before 1935-06-14 are accrued consequences of the code's operation and are not continued operation of the denial; the code's section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with an approved code (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise a consequence of the code, and the held text does not settle whether the resolution's proviso narrowed it for past action. No held source continues the denial after 1935-06-14.

source_notes.date_qualification: Statute of 1933-06-16; its code-enforcement effects ended by the repeal approved 1935-06-14. The repeal is a later event of the denial clause, not its end.
source_notes.reason: Legal effects of an approved code under section 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f). The applicants' obligations after the denial arose from the Lumber and Timber Products Industries code operating through these provisions, which section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed; they are not commands of the denial.
